key: He who stands on his tiptoes does not stand firm; he who stretches his legs does not walk (easily).
s: Two images open a chapter on self-display and self-conceit; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 24, takes the first as one greedy for power and fame, who cannot stand long, and the second as striding over others in self-importance till the many block the way.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 24, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 謂貪權慕名，進取功榮，則不可久立身行道也。 … 自以為貴而跨於人，眾共蔽之，使不得行。
evidence.gloss: (On the one on tiptoe:) it means one who covets power and hankers after fame, pushing forward for merit and glory; he cannot long stand and walk the Tao. (On the one who strides:) thinking himself noble he strides over others; the many together block him, so that he cannot go on.
